C0.quote: 𝑛 voters select a committee of 𝑘 candidates
C0.note: Approval-based multiwinner voting; proportionality axioms and rules (MES) reinterpreted as equilibria of budgeting games.

C1.quote: we characterize prominent proportionality axioms as equilibria of budgeting games
C1.note: Main results are correspondences between budgeting-game equilibria and proportionality axioms (EQ/AX), finite improvement of deviation dynamics (EQ), and existence of strong equilibria via the Tree-Sweep algorithm (EQ/AL).

C2.1.value: approval profile; approval ballots (in the associated budgeting game: relevant resources X_i)
C2.1.quote: is an approval profile, i.e., a vector of approval ballots

C2.2.quote: is an approval profile, i.e., a vector of approval ballots
C2.2.note: In the budgeting game players choose budget allocations, but the voting rules studied (MES, new deviation-based rules) take the approval profile as argument.

C2.3.quote: 𝑛 voters whose preferences are expressed by granting, or withholding,
C2.3.note: Voters' preferences, and in the game players' utilities over relevant resources, are referred to.

C2.4.quote: indicating the subset of alternatives agent 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 approves of
C2.4.note: Approval ballots are described as what agents approve of and are set equal to the players' relevant resources (X_i = A_i); no statement about submission or reporting. In the game, allocations (lambda_i) are separate from X_i, but these are not the ballot input of the voting rule; DIST considered but judged a worse fit.

C3.1.note: Players act strategically in allocating budgets, but no analysis considers approval ballots differing from the relevant/approved sets.

C3.2.loc: Introduction p. 52; Sec. 2 Preliminaries pp. 53-55; Sec. 3 pp. 55-56; Sec. 7 Conclusion p. 69

C4.1.quote: the number of active resources relevant to 𝑖
C4.1.note: Utility of player i is |X_i ∩ out(lambda)|, and in the associated game X_i = A_i, so utility = number of approved elected candidates.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: find committees that satisfy desirable fairness requirements, chief among them being proportionality
C5.1.note: Results characterise the core, EJR, EJR+ and priceability (proportional representation of voter groups).

C5.2.quote: for all ℓ-cohesive groups 𝑆 there is a voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑆
C5.2.note: Axioms are defined on the approval profile A; game utilities use X_i = A_i; no statement relating ballots to held preferences beyond describing approvals as expressing preferences.

VOT.quote_behav: each player 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 is to maximize their utility
VOT.quote_info: budgeting games are infinite normal-form games with a finite set of players
VOT.note: Players of the associated budgeting game are the voters; they strategically allocate budgets (equilibria, coalitional deviations, improving-move dynamics). Their approval ballots are exogenous. Information is never discussed; complete information is only inferable from the normal-form game with no uncertainty.

DES.note: New rules are defined via dynamics, but no designer's choice or objective is modelled.
